title: Types, build tools and warnings

objectives.text: Identify compile, link and runtime failure stages, build a complete C++20 program with explicit diagnostics and distinguish warning cleanliness from correctness.
Derive pre-operation integer range guards and safe signed/unsigned index checks without relying on overflow, late casts or a machine-specific int width.

blocks.markdown: C++ is compiled, and its ordinary integer types have bounded ranges. Do not translate Python integer arithmetic by changing only syntax. Each example here is a complete standalone C++20 source file with its own main function; save and build it separately, not by concatenating all main functions into one file. The app C++ execution capability is not assumed. These blocks are locally compiled teaching examples with app runnable=false until an actual current runner is verified; that is not a learner failure.

For a prepared GCC toolchain, save one example as lesson.cpp and run: `g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror lesson.cpp -o lesson`, then run `./lesson` only if the build succeeded. Record compiler version, language mode, flags and source revision. Flags and diagnostic wording are compiler/version dependent. Here -Werror promotes enabled warnings to errors for a fixed local teaching build; it is not a universal dependency-policy recommendation. -Wall does not mean every warning is enabled.

Preprocessing handles includes/macros; compilation translates a translation unit and checks many language rules; linking resolves definitions across object files/libraries into a program. A one-command g++ build usually drives these stages. `g++ -std=c++20 -c lesson.cpp -o lesson.o` stops before linking and produces an object file, not a directly runnable executable. A missing declaration or invalid narrowing can fail compilation; a declared function with no linked definition can fail linking. A successfully linked program can still reject an input, fail a test, encounter undefined behavior or violate its business contract.

blocks.title: Diagnose the stage before editing random flags

steps.text: `int shares{3.5};` is ill-formed narrowing initialization and must be diagnosed. For these strict GCC builds it is an expected compile rejection, not an executable example.
`int compute(); int main(){return compute();}` can compile to an object because the declaration is present, but fails the normal standalone link when no definition/library is supplied.

Returning a result with the wrong currency can compile and link without warnings. Check units and expected values at runtime/tests; a clean compiler report cannot infer the intended financial contract.

blocks.markdown: Use std::numeric_limits<T>::lowest()/max() to inspect supported bounds rather than assuming int is 32 bits or long is 64 bits. Exact-width aliases such as std::int64_t are available only when the implementation supplies that exact-width type. This lesson uses long long and its queried range. Unsigned arithmetic is modulo its type range after the language conversion/promotion rules; that is defined arithmetic, not evidence that wrapping financial quantities is valid. Signed arithmetic whose result is outside its type range has undefined behavior. A test that once printed a wrapped value does not define it.

For nonnegative long long quantity q and price p, let M be max(). If q=0 the product is 0 without division. Otherwise q>0 and q*p <= M is equivalent to p <= floor(M/q). Check this division inequality BEFORE multiplication. Do not compute q*p and inspect it afterward, and do not expect assigning a product of narrower operands into a wider destination to widen the earlier multiplication. The helper rejects negatives or unrepresentable products with an empty optional, and returns a valid zero as a present value. Integer cents and integer shares imply cents of notional under this declared model.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 2000, then 0, then rejected, then rejected on separate lines. This complete program checks range before multiplication, distinguishes a present zero optional from an empty one, and uses no fixed hard-coded maximum. It does not parse text/JSON, apply fee/tick/lot/FX rules or implement a real broker boundary.

blocks.markdown: An implicit signed-to-unsigned conversion can turn a negative index into a large positive value; mixing signed values with size_t in a comparison requires deliberate treatment. C++20 std::cmp_less compares supported signed/unsigned integer values without that usual-conversion trap. A valid index also requires index>=0 and index<count. Do not silence a warning with a cast until a range proof justifies that cast. Bounds checks are meaningful only while the container/storage and its size remain valid; concurrent mutation is not handled here.

blocks.caption: Expected output: false, true, true, false, 2, 2.5 on separate lines. index=-1 is invalid even though it is mathematically less than count. Integer division 5/2 truncates to 2; converting the operand before division yields 2.5. Casting the already computed integer quotient would only produce 2.0, not recover the lost fraction.

blocks.markdown: Warnings, tests and sanitizers answer different questions. Warning-clean source can contain out-of-bounds access, a dangling observer, data races or a wrong fee policy. Optimize only after correctness contracts and measurements exist; do not suppress a warning merely to make the build green. A clean run on one compiler/target does not prove portable layout, numeric behavior or current app capability. Later lessons cover testing and sanitizers with their own scope.

Independent transfer: implement a checked nonnegative addition helper for cents using the guard b<=M-a after validating a,b>=0. Explain why evaluating a+b first is too late. Keep present zero distinct from failure, test max()+0 and max()+1 without ever evaluating the latter overflowing sum, then compile a separate intentionally narrowing fixture and classify its failure stage.

Sources: [GCC warning options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Warning-Options.html), [numeric_limits](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/numeric_limits.html), [C++20 integer comparison](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/intcmp.html), and [integer type/overflow draft wording](https://eel.is/c++draft/basic.fundamental). The draft is a living language reference, not a claim that every later language feature is supported by the locally tested C++20 compiler. Local build evidence names the exact compiler and flags.

summary: A successful build is evidence for that source/toolchain, not business correctness. Guard bounded integer arithmetic before evaluating it, keep signed/unsigned comparisons deliberate and distinguish compile, link and runtime outcomes.
